title: Licensing risk categorization and onboarding scoring for third‑party models
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Current model onboarding is manual and inconsistent across reviewers. We need an automated, auditable way to surface licensing, restricted-weights, and export-control risks early in the onboarding flow and to assign a normalized risk score that gates downstream steps (QA, legal approval, Dedicated/Private availability).

Goal: Ship a risk-categorization service and UI integration that: (1) inspects provided model metadata + artifacts, (2) computes a licensing & restricted-weights risk score, (3) emits structured signals used by the onboarding workflow (allow, require-attestation, block, require-legal-review), and (4) records provenance/audit info for enterprise customers.

Scope: Automated checks for license type parsing (OSI/OSI-incompatible, custom, unknown), model weights provenance tagging (public, encumbered, restricted by license or export-control), license-to-use compatibility rules (commercial vs internal use only), and basic export-control flagging (e.g., restricted crypto or dual-use model indicators). Excludes in-depth legal contract review and manual exceptions process (these will be surfaced as follow-ups).

Non-goals: Rewriting full legal playbook, adding new license definitions (we will maintain mapping + allow legal to add entries), or performing static code analysis of model weights beyond metadata checks and artifact provenance signatures.
acceptance_criteria: Risk service produces a deterministic score (0-100) and a short human-readable rationale for any uploaded model
Onboarding UI surfaces a clear action: Allow / Needs Attestation / Requires Legal Review / Block
Audit record (who, when, what checks, links to artifacts) persisted and visible in Console for enterprise customers
Automated tests cover license parsing edge cases and at least 10 representative open-source/custom license samples
Legal has signed off on the initial ruleset and exception process
Rollout plan exists with canary cohort (internal accounts) and opt-in for early enterprise testers

implementation_notes: Design a simple extensible taxonomy: license_category (OSS, permissive, reciprocal, proprietary, unknown), weight_provenance (public, third-party-encumbered, private), export_flag (none, crypto, dual-use)
Score composition: license_risk (0-60) + provenance_risk (0-30) + export_risk (0-10). Thresholds: 0-20 allow, 21-50 require attestation, 51-80 require legal review, 81-100 block by default.
Provide a review UI for Legal to add exceptions; exceptions should be tied to model id and recorded in audit logs.

Integration points: Onboarding API (server-side), Console (UI badge & workflows), Dedicated/private provisioning (block if score >=51 unless exception), and telemetry for SLO/latency budget (target <300ms extra for risk check on metadata-only uploads).
